title: Micropersona Templating — Odyssey Notes
content:
Purpose: play with small, highly constrained persona templates that act as lightweight adapters for downstream prompts. Goal is to get robust, style-consistent outputs with minimal context tokens and to catalog brittle failure cases.

Notes-to-self (high level):
- Distinguish micropersona from instruction tuning: micropersona is ephemeral, applied client-side at runtime, tiny token footprint, mostly stylistic and role constraints.
- Focus on: brevity, anchor cues, contradiction-resilience, out-of-domain fallbacks.
- Track token cost impact of each persona variant (rough estimation: 8–24 tokens for persona header).

=== Quick taxonomy ===
1) Tone anchors — adjectives to bias style (e.g., encouraging, terse, formal).
2) Knowledge anchors — role labels + assumed knowledge scope (e.g., "AI system with up-to-date product knowledge" vs "generalist assistant, no external data").
3) Safety anchors — explicit refusal patterns.
4) Fallback heuristics — what to do on unknown: ask clarifying question / provide best-guess / defer to human.

=== Micropersona template prototypes ===
Template A: Minimalist-guide (6–10 tokens):
  "You are a concise engineering reviewer."
Use: code reviews, terse summaries.
Observations: reduces verbosity often, but model will sometimes overcompress and drop necessary edge-case warnings.

Template B: Contextual-synth (18 tokens):
  "You are a helpful product analyst. Only use the facts in the prompt; if unsure, say 'insufficient info'. Keep answers in bullet points and include 1 risk."
Use: product brief summarization with conservative stance.
Observations: adding 'Only use the facts in the prompt' helps reduce hallucinations but model occasionally fabricates a plausible sounding risk. Need stronger refusal phrasing.

Template C: Persona-with-frame (24 tokens):
  "You are 'Maya', a UX researcher with 3 quick take constraints: 1) one-line insight; 2) one supporting observation; 3) one action suggestion. Avoid technical metrics."
Use: convert qualitative notes to structured outputs.
Observations: naming persona 'Maya' occasionally yields unexpected narrative flourishes (backstory). Use anonymized role labels to avoid story drift.

=== Experiments (runs) ===
Experiment 1 — Minimalist-guide on code diff summary (gpt-3.5-ish model):
Prompt: 'Diff: added caching layer, potential stale reads. Tests: none added. Question: summarize.'
Output summary: 2 sentences, missed noting lack of tests.
Notes: need explicit checklist anchor: 'always call out tests coverage & perf regressions' or include few-shot that shows desired output shape.

Experiment 2 — Contextual-synth on ambiguous product note:
Prompt: 'Launch date tentative; user will be unfamiliar. Bullet out launch communications risk.'
Output: gave 3 risks, one invented competitor name.
Fix: add explicit refusal token 'do not invent competitor names; if none provided, write "unknown"'.

Experiment 3 — Persona-with-frame for research notes extraction:
Prompt: 3 raw quotes from usability sessions.
Output: produced 'Maya said...' style attributions.
Fix: replace persona name with role label, add 'Do not invent quotes or attributes'.

=== Few-shot sets (small curated exemplars) ===
Approach: pair each micropersona with 1–3 exemplars that show negative/positive examples. Keep exemplar tokens under 100 combined.
Example pair for Template B:
  Example 1 (good): Q: 'What are top concerns for feature X?' A: '- Privacy: users unclear about data flows
- Onboarding: 2 unclear steps
- Risk: might increase support tickets'
  Example 2 (bad): includes invented metrics and competitor references.
Observations: The 'bad' exemplar as negative example reduces hallucination frequency in A/B test.

=== Failure catalog (selected, reproducible) ===
- Name hallucination: when persona uses a plausible human name or backstory (fix: "Do not generate personal names or stories").
- Metric hallucination: invents % improvements (fix: explicit 'no numbers unless given; mark as unknown otherwise').
- Overconcision loss: trimming critical caveats (fix: 'always include a 'risks & unknowns' section').
- Token bleeding: persona header pushes out prompts when hard token limit; higher truncation of user examples.

=== Oddities observed ===
- Positioning the persona as a named character increases narrative creativity. Avoid names for engineering/product outputs.
- Adding explicit refusal words like 'do not invent' is helpful but sometimes ignored unless followed by penalty phrasing ("If invented, mark as 'unsure'").
- A single exemplar that contains 'bad example' phrasing seems to act as a guide more than deterrent on some models — might need multiple negative exemplars.

=== Quick recipes (copyable) ===
1) Low-cost conservative summary (tokens: ~12):
  Persona: "You are a concise analyst. Only use supplied facts. If missing, reply 'insufficient info'"
  Few-shot: 1 example showing 'insufficient info' + 1 good example.
2) On-device micropersona for chat (tokens: ~20):
  Persona: "Assistant persona: friendly, 2-claim max per answer, cite only prompt facts."
  Post-processing: if response contains new entity names that aren't in prompt, redact to 'unknown'.

=== TODO / experiments to run ===
- [ ] Systematically sweep persona token lengths (6,12,18,24) against a fixed testset (30 prompts). Measure hallucination rate & average token length of replies.
- [ ] Test negative-exemplar counts: 0,1,3. Evaluate hallucination delta.
- [ ] Create 'refusal amplifiers' by adding short rule + punishment phrasing and test effect.
- [ ] Try soft anchoring: instead of 'Do not invent X', say 'Prefer not to invent X; if unavoidable, mark as unsure' — measure differences.
- [ ] Add a tiny verifier-stage: prompt a separate verifier to flag invented entities (cheap composite check).

=== Notes for integration into prompt library ===
- Store persona template + 2 exemplars + canonical postprocessing rule as a single library item. Metadata: token_cost_estimate, primary_use_case, failure_modes.
- Make 'refusal baseline' explicit in metadata so product teams can choose tradeoff.

=== Random field notes / rants ===
- "Naming personas is fun but toxic for reproducibility."
- "We keep adding 'only use prompt facts' and the model still summarizes like it read the whole internet. Why?"
- "Small models are surprisingly obedient to negative examples; big models sometimes invert the instruction pattern."

=== Recent runs (short log) ===
2024-10-03: ran 30 prompts w/ Template A vs baseline. Hallucinations dropped 6% but missing caveats rose 18%.
2024-10-18: negative exemplar added to Template B — hallucinations dropped 14%.
2024-10-29: added strict 'no numbers' clause; model substituted qualitative hedges instead of inventing numbers.

References / links: see linked_artifacts above (issue 324 is the tracking ticket). Also cross-ref LINEAR-5123 for evaluation harness.

If I return to this later: create a reproducible harness (small pytest file) that loads persona headers, attaches few-shots, and computes precision/recall of invented entities vs gold. Keep token budget and runtime constraints in mind.

End of notebook.

Actionable next note: port Template B + 3 exemplars into prompt-library under key "micropersona.product-brief.v1" and add a short 'postprocess redact function' in client SDK that strips invented entity tokens.
